properties.statement: [BL-140] designation: required means "supplied from outside" and unprovided_interface does not read it, so declaring the truth does not stop the alarm
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Found 2026-08-01 by an /adopt pass over music_graph, a ~11k-LOC Python research repo taken from an empty graph to 134 nodes / 379 edges. Reported in that project's own reflow2_feedback.txt.* Verified in source 2026-08-01: detect.rs:1165 counts incoming PROVIDES and incoming CONSUMES and never consults Interface.designation. The schema already carries the answer the detector is asking for. designation: required is documented in structure.yaml as *\"this design NEEDS one of these FROM OUTSIDE; it is the half that was missing until 2026-07-30, and without it a design could say what it offered but not what it needed\"*. Two interfaces marked required (ifc:wav-audio, ifc:fluidsynth-cli) still fired *\"Nothing supplies X, but N parts rely on it\"* at severity 0.72 \u2014 the second-highest gaps in the run. The workaround is the finding: the reporter invented a boundary Component (cmp:external-fluidsynth) purely to satisfy the detector, and named it correctly \u2014 *\"that is modelling for the tool, not for the truth\"*, which is the failure mode [BL-42] and [BL-23] both exist to prevent. Fix shape: an Interface designated required or both has already answered the question; it should not raise unprovided_interface. The counterweight that must survive: an internal interface with no provider is still a real break, and internal is the DEFAULT \u2014 so this must key on the designation actually being required/both, never on silence. Size S", "origin": "Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-140 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: S."}
